findings.evidence: p.67 (Ch 3 §3.6.2): "Wan2.2 A14B is a useful counterexample to treating every mixture of experts as per-token top-k routing: its high-noise and low-noise experts are selected from the current timestep rather than by a per-token gate, at about 27B total and about 14B active parameters as published (Wan2.2 source). [1P][FACT]"
findings.issue: Vague first-party source attribution. The source is cited only as '(Wan2.2 source)' with [1P][FACT], which does not name a specific document, URL, or revision. Compare with p.56 in the same chapter which gives precise provenance: '(Wan2.2 sampling loop, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28.)'. The convention requires [1P] to identify a 'first-party source' — 'Wan2.2 source' is too generic to be independently verified.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace '(Wan2.2 source)' with the specific first-party source identifier used on p.56, e.g. '(Wan2.2 source, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28)' or the appropriate model card / repository reference.

findings.evidence: p.65 (Ch 3 §3.6.1): "Muse Glimmer 30B ([2°][FACT], source: Meta model card, via vLLM-Recipes) is a dense 29.6B local-agentic model that runs in ~18 GB at ~5-bit weights [2°]."
findings.issue: Contradictory source attribution: the citation names 'Meta model card' as the source but tags it [2°] (second-hand) because it was accessed 'via vLLM-Recipes.' If the actual access path was through vLLM-Recipes (an intermediary), then vLLM-Recipes is the source, not Meta's model card. Calling a Meta model card '[2°]' (second-hand) is inconsistent — either it is first-party [1P] accessed directly, or it is second-hand [2°] from vLLM-Recipes. The current attribution reads as both.
findings.fix_instruction: Either change to '[2°][FACT], source: vLLM-Recipes (citing Meta model card)' to correctly identify the actual access path, or change to '[1P][FACT], source: Meta model card, URL: <direct URL>' if the model card was accessed directly.

findings.evidence: Compute ratio vs dense 70B ~0.183× (~5.5× less) (12.8B × 2) ÷ (70B × 2) = 25.6 GFLOP ÷ 140 GFLOP; the ratio is against the canonical 70B dense reference, not against a dense model of the challenger's own ~47B total — against that baseline the saving is ~3.7× (12.8B ÷ 47B ≈ 27%)
findings.issue: Two different 'savings' multipliers for the same MoE comparison circulate through Ch. 3: ~5.5× (against the 70B dense baseline) and ~3.7× (against a same-total dense baseline). Table 3-2's row reads 'Compute ratio vs dense 70B ~0.183× (~5.5× less)' while §3.3.3's prose says 'the relative saving is about 5.5× versus the canonical 70B dense comparison, not 20× or 30×' and 'It is also 12.8/47 ≈ 27% of a hypothetical dense model of the same 47B total'. The Ch. 3 mini-case (p. 69) then restates 'a ~5.5× reduction in compute per token'. The ~3.7× figure appears only once, in a derivation cell, and is never given a name. Three presentations of one comparison with two unreconciled multipliers.
findings.fix_instruction: Fix one pair of numbers and name them: 'vs the canonical 70B dense baseline: 5.5× less compute; vs a same-total (47B) dense model: 3.7× less'. State both in §3.3.3 and in Table 3-2's derivation cell, and use the named pair in the mini-case.

findings.issue: Provenance-status mismatch at the section level. The section heading labels the whole worked example '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]', but the section's first sentence states 'Its published model card gives 46.7B total and 12.9B active parameters per token [1P][FACT]' — a first-party fact — while the table rows below carry '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]'. The heading's [ASSUMPTION] tag therefore mis-describes a section whose primary parameter counts are [1P][FACT] and whose rows are [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]. The book's stated rule (Preface p. 18: 'A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes') does not allow a heading-level [ASSUMPTION] to cover a table whose rows are [DERIVED].
findings.fix_instruction: Re-tag the section heading to state the per-row split explicitly, e.g. '§3.3.2. MoE model representative (Mixtral 8x7B class) — model card [1P][FACT]; component-derived arithmetic [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]', and keep the per-row tags as they are. Apply the same treatment to §3.3.1 ('[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]'), which currently leaves the reader unsure whether the 140 GB row is an assumption or a derivation.

findings.evidence: Dense 70B: KV cache ≈ 12.06 GB at 8-bit (1.31 MB per token × 9,200 tokens) or ≈ 24.1 GB at FP16 (2.62 MB per token × 9,200 tokens; the key/value storage pattern is discussed in Ch 7)
findings.issue: Two defects in one row. (1) The derivation multiplies the *rounded* 1.31 MB and 2.62 MB constants (9,200 × 1.31 MB = 12.052 GB → '12.06'; 9,200 × 2.62 MB = 24.104 GB → '24.1'), i.e. the printed derivations do not reproduce the printed results: 9,200 × 1.31 MB = 12.052 GB, not 12.06 GB, and 9,200 × 2.62 MB = 24.104 GB, which rounds to 24.1 ✓ by luck, not by construction. Ch. 1 (p. 27) states the book's convention is to derive from the exact byte count, so this row's derivation contradicts the stated convention. (2) The row carries '[canonical scenario][DERIVED]' for a figure the sentence itself frames as derived from the canonical geometry — but the 8-bit figure is a precision variant of the canonical FP16 constant, and the canonical scenario's KV precision is FP16 (Table 4-2). Presenting the 8-bit figure under the [canonical scenario] tag implies it is part of the canonical set when it is a variant.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-derive the row from exact bytes: '9,200 × 2,621,440 B = 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB (FP16); 9,200 × 1,310,720 B = 12,058,624,000 B ≈ 12.06 GB (8-bit)'. Tag the 8-bit figure [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] or explicitly '(FP8 variant of the canonical FP16 constant)', consistent with Ch. 1's treatment.

findings.evidence: PDF p. 58: "The 70B dense full-MHA model below is a constructed teaching reference... not a named vendor model — so its geometry is [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] and its arithmetic is [canonical scenario][DERIVED]. Reserve [1P] for a named, traceable first-party model specification."
findings.issue: Conflicting definitions between chapters. Chapter 4 Table 4-1 (PDF p. 79) explicitly lists the 'Model baseline: Dense 70B' and assigns it the tag `[canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] reference model`. It does not declare the model to be hypothetical. Yet Chapter 3 asserts that the 70B model is constructed and instructs readers not to use `[1P]` for it, creating semantic confusion about whether the canonical baseline is an actual deployable architecture or a purely pedagogical ghost model.
findings.fix_instruction: Clarify the status of the canonical model in Chapter 4 Table 4-1. If the 70B is a purely constructed geometry, the text in Table 4-1 must state so explicitly, or the `[1P]` reservation rule in Chapter 3 needs to be softened to reflect that the canonical baseline maps directly to a class of dense models.

findings.evidence: PDF p. 63 (Printed Page 43): "For the canonical 80L/8192H full-MHA shape... the KV cache memory is the same either way — plan accordingly; a model with a smaller or GQA shape (like the ~47B challenger, ~0.6 GB at 8-bit) needs fewer bytes, but that is its shape, not its routing."
findings.issue: Semantic drift in figure data. The text on p. 63 states the challenger has ~0.6 GB at 8-bit. However, checking Figure 3.4 (PDF p. 72) and Table 3-3 (PDF p. 74), the MoE KV cache at FP16 is explicitly listed as ~1.2 GB, and at 8-bit as ~0.60 GB. The text on page 63 says '~0.6 GB at 8-bit', which matches, but page 49 text says 'the challenger’s own 32L/4096H GQA shape would need only ~0.6 GB (8-bit) / ~1.2 GB (FP16)'. This is mathematically correct, but earlier on page 43, text states '~0.6 GB (8-bit) / ~1.2 GB (FP16)' which is also correct. There is no arithmetic error, but there's a semantic conflict on p. 43 where it claims 'a model with a smaller or GQA shape ... needs fewer bytes'. If the user assumes the 'smaller shape' inherently includes a 32-layer limit, they miss the 80-layer limit of canonical 70B. This should be a 'reduced-width per-token' family, not just smaller shape.
findings.fix_instruction: No actual defect found after verification. Withdrawing.
